about: exp90 harder rule questions, hand-written from the state-policy-docs corpus (2026-10-12): applied rules with household facts and arithmetic, dates and state implementation lag, exceptions, two-rule combinations. options[0] correct (shuffled at build). Every evidence phrase must appear in a source's text on as_of.

questions.stem: A household has $140 in monthly gross income and $90 in a checking account. Is it entitled to expedited service?
options: Yes: gross income under $150 and liquid resources of $100 or less
No: gross income must be under $100
Only if it is a migrant or seasonal farmworker household
Only if its rent exceeds its income
evidence: households with less than $150 in monthly gross income
do not exceed $100

questions.stem: A household has $160 in monthly gross income and $50 in savings. Its rent is $800 a month and its utility allowance is $300. Is it entitled to expedited service?
options: Yes: its income plus liquid resources ($210) is less than its rent and utilities ($1,100)
No: its gross income is not under $150
No: its liquid resources must be under $25
Only if every member is elderly or disabled
Only if it applied after the 15th of the month
evidence: combined monthly gross income and liquid resources are less than the household's monthly rent or mortgage, and utilities

questions.stem: A household has $140 in monthly gross income and $250 in a bank account. Its rent and utilities total $300 a month. Is it entitled to expedited service?
options: No: its liquid resources exceed $100 and its income plus resources ($390) exceed its rent and utilities
Yes: its gross income is under $150
Yes: any household under $500 in resources qualifies
Only if it has a member over 60
evidence: do not exceed $100
combined monthly gross income and liquid resources are less than the household's monthly rent or mortgage, and utilities

questions.stem: A household's monthly gross income is $900 and it has $400 in savings. Its rent is $1,100 and its utility allowance is $350. Is it entitled to expedited service?
options: Yes: its income plus liquid resources ($1,300) is less than its rent and utilities ($1,450)
evidence: combined monthly gross income and liquid resources are less than the household's monthly rent or mortgage, and utilities

questions.stem: A household's only elderly member pays $210 a month in unreimbursed medical costs. What is the excess medical deduction?
evidence: medical expenses in excess of $35 per month

questions.stem: A 40-year-old household member who is neither elderly nor disabled pays $300 a month in medical costs; no one else has medical costs. What is the excess medical deduction?
options: $0: only elderly or disabled members' costs count
evidence: incurred by any household member who is elderly or disabled

questions.stem: A household with no elderly or disabled member has $600 a month of income after all other deductions and $1,500 a month in shelter costs. What is its excess shelter deduction in the 48 contiguous states?
evidence: monthly shelter expenses in excess of 50 percent
cannot exceed the maximum shelter deduction limit

questions.stem: A household that includes a disabled member has $600 a month of income after all other deductions and $1,500 a month in shelter costs. What is its excess shelter deduction?
options: $1,200: no cap for a household with an elderly or disabled member
evidence: monthly shelter expenses in excess of 50 percent
if the household does not contain an elderly or disabled member

questions.stem: A household with no elderly or disabled member has $1,000 a month of income after all other deductions and $900 in shelter costs. What is its excess shelter deduction?
evidence: monthly shelter expenses in excess of 50 percent

questions.stem: Under the Food and Nutrition Act as in force on that date, can a household's monthly internet service fee be counted in its excess shelter deduction?
options: Only for households with school-age children
Only if the state's utility allowance does not include it
evidence: any service fee associated with internet connection shall not be used in computing the excess shelter expense deduction

questions.stem: Under the Food and Nutrition Act as in force on that date, is a 56-year-old able-bodied adult without dependents subject to the ABAWD time limit?
options: No: in fiscal year 2025 the exception covers people over 55
Yes: there is no age exception
evidence: fiscal year 2025 and each fiscal year thereafter over 55 years of age

questions.stem: Under the Food and Nutrition Act as in force on that date, is a 54-year-old able-bodied adult without dependents subject to the ABAWD time limit?
options: Yes: in fiscal year 2025 the age exception covers only people over 55
No: the exception covers people over 49
No: the exception covers people over 50
No: the time limit was repealed
evidence: fiscal year 2025 and each fiscal year thereafter over 55 years of age

questions.stem: Under the Food and Nutrition Act as in force on that date, is a 60-year-old able-bodied adult without dependents subject to the ABAWD time limit?
options: Yes: the age exception now covers only people over 65
No: the exception covers people over 55
No: the exception covers people 60 and older
No: the exception covers people over 59
No: the time limit applies only under 50
evidence: under 18, or over 65, years of age

questions.stem: Under the Food and Nutrition Act as in force on that date, a parent's youngest child in the household is 15. Is the parent excepted from the ABAWD time limit because of the child?
options: No: the exception covers responsibility for a dependent child under 14
Yes: any dependent child of any age qualifies
evidence: dependent child under 14 years of age

questions.stem: Under the Food and Nutrition Act as in force on that date, which of these is still listed as an exception to the ABAWD time limit?
options: A 22-year-old who aged out of foster care
evidence: (e) a pregnant woman

questions.stem: Under the Food and Nutrition Act as in force on that date, which of these people is excepted from the ABAWD time limit?
options: A 23-year-old who was in foster care at age 18
A 30-year-old who was in foster care at age 15 only
A 45-year-old who works 10 hours a week
evidence: an individual who is 24 years of age or younger and who was in foster care

questions.stem: An able-bodied adult without dependents works 15 hours a week and volunteers in a state work program 6 hours a week. Do they meet the ABAWD work requirement?
options: Yes: work and a work program can be combined to reach 20 hours a week
No: they must work 20 hours in a job alone
No: they must work 30 hours a week
Yes: any work at all meets the requirement
evidence: any combination of working and participating in a work program for a total of 20

questions.stem: In California, a CalFresh application is received on May 29, 2026 and approved on June 8, 2026. Under which ABAWD exemption criteria is the applicant screened?
options: The criteria in force on the approval date
evidence: applications received before june 1, 2026 must be screened under the pre- hr1 rules

questions.stem: In California, an ongoing CalFresh household's recertification was due in May 2026 and its new certification period starts June 1, 2026. Which ABAWD exemption criteria apply at that recertification?
options: The H.R. 1 criteria, because the new period starts June 1
The criteria in the county's waiver
evidence: ongoing households with a recertification due in may 2026 must be screened using pre-hr1 exemption criteria

questions.stem: In California, a household reports on June 3, 2026 that a new member joined. Under which ABAWD exemption criteria is the new member screened?
options: The H.R. 1 criteria, even if other members have not had an H.R. 1 screening
The pre-H.R. 1 criteria, because the household's other members were screened under them
No screening until the next recertification
The criteria in force when the household first applied
evidence: new household members must be screened under the new hr1 rules even if the other household members have not received an hr1 compliant screening

questions.stem: In California, a household reports on May 20, 2026 that a new member joined. Under which ABAWD exemption criteria is the new member screened?
options: No screening until the next recertification
The criteria in the federal statute as of that date
evidence: if the household reports a change in household composition before june 1, 2026, the new household member must be screened under the pre-hr1 rules

questions.stem: In California, can a county assign an ABAWD countable month for March 2026?
options: No: no countable months may be assigned before June 1, 2026
Yes: the new statewide clock started January 1, 2026
Only in counties without a waiver
Only for applicants, not ongoing households
evidence: no countable months may be assigned prior to june 1, 2026

questions.stem: Is Alpine County, California covered by an ABAWD time limit waiver in November 2026?
options: No: its waiver expired October 31, 2026 and it was not included in the new waiver
Yes: the waiver runs through October 31, 2027
Yes: all California counties are waived
evidence: alpine county's current waiver will expire on october 31, 2026

questions.stem: In California, a CalFresh application is received on March 28, 2026 and processed on April 3, 2026. Which noncitizen eligibility criteria apply?
options: The H.R. 1 criteria, because it was processed after April 1
The H.R. 1 criteria, because H.R. 1 took effect July 4, 2025
The criteria in effect on the interview date
evidence: any application received before april 1, 2026, must be processed under the pre-h.r

questions.stem: In California, when do the H.R. 1 noncitizen rules first apply to an ongoing household?
options: At its recertification, starting with recertifications due in April 2026 (effective May 1, 2026)
Never; they apply only to new applicants
evidence: this applies to recertifications due in april 2026 with an effective date of may 1, 2026, and onwards

questions.stem: In California, will a lawful permanent resident who was eligible for CalFresh before April 1, 2026 remain eligible after April 1, 2026, regardless of how they obtained that status?
options: No, unless they obtained status through employment
No, they lose eligibility at the next recertification
Only if they have 40 work quarters
evidence: will all lprs who were calfresh eligible prior to april 1, 2026, remain eligible after april 1, 2026, regardless of how they obtained lpr status? answer 2: yes

questions.stem: In California, from June 1, 2026, may a county require a parolee to have been paroled for at least one year to receive California Food Assistance Program (CFAP) benefits?
options: Yes, but only for new applicants
evidence: must not impose a one-year parole duration requirement

questions.stem: In California, a household with a student in a UC bachelor's program has a recertification due in June 2026. When does the new LPIE process apply to it?
options: For the certification period effective July 1, 2026
evidence: recertification due in june 2026 with an effective date of july 1, 2026

questions.stem: In California, when does an ongoing CalWORKs/CalFresh family first get the AB 42 exemption for higher-education grants and scholarships?
options: At its next SAR 7 or recertification after March 1, 2026
evidence: at their next sar 7 or recertification/redetermination after march 1, 2026

questions.stem: In California, does the AB 320 income exemption change a benefit determination made in May 2026?
options: No: it does not apply retroactively to determinations made before July 1, 2026
Yes: it applies back to January 1, 2026
Yes: counties must recompute all 2026 benefits
Only if the household requests it
evidence: this policy does not apply retroactively to benefit determinations made prior to july 1, 2026

questions.stem: Since when has California operated its CalFresh Standard Medical Deduction demonstration project?
evidence: beginning october 1, 2017

questions.stem: How does California CalFresh treat Medicare Advantage supplemental benefits (such as plan reimbursements)?
options: They are counted as unearned income
They are counted as earned income
They are counted as a resource
They reduce the medical deduction dollar for dollar
evidence: these medical reimbursements are excluded from income for calfresh purposes

questions.stem: Through when are California counties approved to operate the Early Denial Waiver?
evidence: through april 30, 2029

questions.stem: For how long did FNS hold states harmless in Quality Control for misapplying the H.R. 1 utility allowance (LIHEAP) change?
evidence: fns will hold states harmless for quality control (qc) purposes for 120 days from the implementation date of july 4, 2025

questions.stem: Under the Food and Nutrition Act as in force on that date, a household with no elderly or disabled member received a $25 LIHEAP payment last winter. Must the state give it the heating and cooling utility allowance on that basis?
options: Yes: a LIHEAP payment over $20 in the current or prior 12 months qualifies any household
No: only households with an elderly or disabled member qualify
No: LIHEAP no longer affects the allowance
Only if it pays heating costs directly
evidence: shall be made available to households that received a payment
greater than $20 annually

questions.stem: Under the Food and Nutrition Act as in force on that date, a household with no elderly or disabled member received a $25 LIHEAP payment last winter. Must the state give it the heating and cooling utility allowance on that basis?
options: No: the LIHEAP rule now covers only households with an elderly or disabled member
Yes: any LIHEAP payment over $20 qualifies
evidence: shall be made available to households with an elderly or disabled member that received a payment

questions.stem: Under the Food and Nutrition Act as in force on that date, a household received a $15 LIHEAP payment last year. Does that payment by itself entitle it to the heating and cooling utility allowance?
options: No: the payment must be greater than $20
Yes: payments of $10 or more qualify
Only if it has an elderly member
evidence: greater than $20 annually

questions.stem: Under the Food and Nutrition Act as in force on that date, once the cost share applies, what share of benefit costs does a state with a payment error rate of exactly 10.0% pay?
evidence: equal to or greater than 10 percent

questions.stem: Under the Food and Nutrition Act as in force on that date, once the cost share applies, what share of benefit costs does a state with a payment error rate of 5.9% pay?
evidence: less than 6 percent

questions.stem: Under the Food and Nutrition Act as in force on that date, does a state with a 12% payment error rate pay a share of benefit costs in fiscal year 2027?
options: No: the state share begins in fiscal year 2028
evidence: beginning in fiscal year 2028

questions.stem: Under the Food and Nutrition Act as in force on that date, once the cost share applies, what share of benefit costs does a state with a payment error rate of 7.99% pay?
evidence: equal to or greater than 6 percent but less than 8 percent

questions.stem: A 19-year-old enrolled half-time at a community college works 15 hours a week, has no children, and meets no other exemption. Can they get SNAP?
options: No: they need 20 paid work hours a week or another exemption
Yes: half-time students are not covered by the student rule
Yes: community college students are exempt
evidence: employed for a minimum of 20 hours per week

questions.stem: A 25-year-old enrolled full-time cares for her 8-year-old child, and the state has found adequate child care is available. Is she exempt from the student rule because of the child?
options: No: for a child 6 to 11, the exemption applies only when adequate child care is not available
Yes: any parent of a child under 12 is exempt
Yes: any parent of a child under 18 is exempt
Yes: full-time students with children are always exempt
evidence: is under age 12 when the state agency has determined that adequate child care is not available

questions.stem: A 30-year-old student enrolled half-time cares for a 4-year-old household member. Is the student exempt from the student rule?
options: Yes: responsible for a dependent household member under 6
No: only parents of children under 1 are exempt
No: the child must be under 2
Only if child care is unavailable
Only if they also work 20 hours
evidence: be responsible for the care of a dependent household member under the age of 6

questions.stem: A 52-year-old enrolled full-time in a graduate program, not working, applies for SNAP. Does the student rule bar them?
options: No: students age 50 or older are exempt
Yes: graduate students are never eligible
Yes: they must work 20 hours a week
Yes: the age exemption ends at 50
evidence: be age 17 or younger or age 50 or older

questions.stem: A student approved for federal work study expects to work during the term. When does their work-study exemption begin?
options: The month the school term begins or the month work study is approved, whichever is later
The day they first get paid
At the start of the calendar year
Only after they work 20 hours in a week
evidence: the exemption shall begin with the month in which the school term begins or the month work study is approved, whichever is later

questions.stem: A person is found to have committed a second intentional Program violation (no trafficking or other special case). How long are they disqualified?
evidence: for a period of twenty-four months upon the second occasion

questions.stem: A person is found to have committed a third intentional Program violation. How long are they disqualified?
evidence: permanently for the third occasion

questions.stem: A person fails to comply with SNAP work requirements for the second time and complies again right away. What is the shortest federal disqualification period?
options: None, if they comply right away
evidence: for the second occurrence, until the later of
three months

questions.stem: For a third occurrence of noncompliance with SNAP work requirements, which disqualification may a state choose?
evidence: at the option of the state agency, permanently

questions.stem: A state discovers an intentional Program violation that began 30 months ago. How far back must the claim be calculated?
options: To the month the violation first occurred
Only to the start of the current certification period
evidence: for an ipv claim, the claim must be calculated back to the month the act of ipv first occurred

questions.stem: A state discovers an overpayment that started 8 years ago. What is the oldest period a claim may include?
options: No amounts more than six years before the state became aware of it
evidence: don't include any amounts that occurred more than six years before you became aware of the overpayment

questions.stem: A county error cost a household benefits for 18 months before the household asked for restoration. How many months of lost benefits must be restored (absent a rule allowing longer)?
options: None; only future benefits are adjusted
evidence: benefits shall be restored for not more than twelve months prior to whichever of the following occurred first

questions.stem: A married couple live together but buy and cook food separately. How must they apply?
options: As one household: spouses must be in the same household
As two households, since they buy food separately
As two households only if one is elderly
As one household only if they have children
evidence: (i) spouses

questions.stem: A 23-year-old lives with his parents and buys and prepares his food separately. Must he be in his parents' household?
options: No: the required combination covers people under 22
Yes: adult children living with parents must be included
Yes, if he is a student
No: only people under 18 are covered
evidence: a person under 22 years of age who is living with his or her natural or adoptive parent(s)

questions.stem: A 16-year-old (not a foster child) lives with and is under the parental control of her grandmother, who receives SNAP. Must she be in her grandmother's household?
options: No: only parents and children must apply together
No: only if the grandmother is her legal guardian
Only if she has no income
evidence: a child (other than a foster child) under 18 years of age who lives with and is under the parental control of a household member other than his or her parent

questions.stem: An employer provides an employee free housing instead of a cash payment. How is the value of the housing treated for SNAP?
options: Excluded: it is an in-kind benefit
evidence: in-kind benefits are those for which no monetary payment is made on behalf of the household and include meals, clothing, housing

questions.stem: A household receives a payment that reimburses its normal rent. Is the reimbursement excluded from income?
options: No: reimbursements for normal living expenses such as rent are a gain or benefit and are counted
Yes, if paid by a charity
Only if paid directly to the landlord
evidence: reimbursements for normal household living expenses such as rent or mortgage, personal clothing, or food eaten at home are a gain or benefit and, therefore, are not excluded

questions.stem: A household member rents out a property and actively manages it 25 hours a week on average. How is the rental income treated?
evidence: income derived from the rental property shall be considered earned income only if a member of the household is actively engaged in the management of the property at least an average of 20 hours a week

questions.stem: A household receives payments from a roomer (not a foster care boarder). How are those payments treated?
options: As a reduction of shelter costs
evidence: payments from a roomer or boarder, except foster care boarders, shall also be considered self-employment income

questions.stem: A household member applied for a new job but it is uncertain whether or when the job will start. How is the possible income treated at certification?
options: Not counted, because the amount or timing is uncertain
Counted at half the expected wage
Counted at the state minimum wage
Counted only for the first month
evidence: that portion of the household's income that is uncertain shall not be counted

questions.stem: A state uses the child support deduction. A household member voluntarily sends money to a non-household child without any legal obligation. Is it deductible?
options: No: only legally obligated child support is deductible
Yes: any support to a child is deductible
Only if the child is under 6
evidence: legally obligated child support payments paid by a household member to or for a nonhousehold member

questions.stem: A state uses the child support deduction. Are alimony payments a household member makes to a former spouse deductible under it?
options: Yes, up to the standard deduction
Only if the former spouse has children
evidence: alimony payments made to or for a nonhousehold member shall not be in

questions.stem: A household applies on April 10 and contains a member who is 59 on that date but turns 60 on April 25. Which income test applies for the application month?
options: The net income test only (as for households with an elderly member)
Both gross and net income tests
evidence: fifty-nine years old on the date of application, but who will become sixty before the end of the month of application

questions.stem: A household member is a student whose earnings are excluded because of age, and she turns 18 during the month of application. When are her earnings counted?
options: Starting the month after the month of application
Never, while she is a student
evidence: the state agency shall exclude the student's earnings in the month of application and count the student's earnings in the following month

questions.stem: An eligible one-person household applies mid-month. Does the minimum benefit guarantee apply to its prorated first month?
options: No: the minimum benefit applies except during an initial month
Yes: the minimum benefit always applies
Only if the household is elderly
Only if the prorated amount is over $10
evidence: except during an initial month, all eligible one-person and two-person households shall receive minimum monthly allotments

questions.stem: A state uses a standard 30-day month. A household applies on the 31st. For proration, it is treated as applying on which day?
evidence: a household applying on the 31st of a month will be treated as though it applied on the 30th of the month

questions.stem: A simplified-reporting household of 3 had a fourth member join after certification. Which household size's gross income limit does it use to decide whether it must report higher income?
options: 3, the size at its most recent certification
No limit; it reports only at recertification
evidence: the household shall use the monthly gross income limit for the household size that existed at the time of its most recent certification or recertification

questions.stem: Between periodic reports, when must a simplified-reporting household report a change in income?
options: When its monthly gross income exceeds the gross income limit (130% of poverty) for its size
Whenever income changes by $50 or more
Whenever income changes by $100 or more
evidence: must report when its monthly gross income exceeds the monthly gross income limit

questions.stem: A state certifies a household whose adult members are all elderly for 24 months. What contact must the state have during that period?
options: At least one contact every 12 months
evidence: the state agency must have at least one contact with each household every 12 months

questions.stem: An applicant's employer refuses to cooperate and no other verification of the applicant's wages is available. What does the eligibility worker do?
options: Use the best available information to determine an amount for certification
Delay certification until the employer responds
evidence: the eligibility worker shall determine an amount to be used for certification purposes based on the best available information

questions.stem: How is the SNAP Quality Control error tolerance threshold adjusted each year?
options: By the percentage change in the Thrifty Food Plan
By the Consumer Price Index for shelter
By the change in the national error rate
By the change in the standard deduction
evidence: this qc tolerance level shall be adjusted annually by the percentage by which the thrifty food plan

questions.stem: What was the Quality Control error tolerance threshold for fiscal year 2014?
evidence: for fiscal year 2014, only variances that exceed $37.00 (the threshold)

questions.stem: Which of these people is exempt from the general SNAP work requirements because of age?
options: A 17-year-old head of household not in school
evidence: a person younger than 16 years of age or a person 60 years of age or older

questions.stem: A 17-year-old who is not the head of household attends high school half-time. Are they exempt from the general SNAP work requirements?
options: No: only people under 16 are exempt
Only if a parent is exempt
evidence: a person age 16 or 17 who is not the head of a household or who is attending school
